text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuanian prosecutors say they have found definite suspects for the explosion 10 months ago at the office of leading newspaper Lietuvos rytas. They also accuse former interior minister Romasis Vaitiekunas of hindering the investigation when it began.

- Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Stankevicius and Finance Minister Algimantas Krizhinauskas met the association of local governments and agreed on taking loans from the World Bank for paying their debts to the energy system, which stood at 96 million litas at the start of September.

- Right-wing parliament opposition leader Vytautas Landsbergis accused Stankevicius of giving too favourable terms for securities house Merill Lynch to buy 200 million litas of government T-bills with 22 percent interest rate. He said there might have been banks in Lithuania satisfied with 15 percent the same deal. Landsbergis alleged during a press conference on Monday that Stankevicius may have personally profited from the transaction.
- Law and order ministries are to draw up a plan to fight smuggling in ten days, it was decided during a meeting between the ministries and President Algirdas Brazauskas.
- Klaipeda District court started a bankruptcy case against the insolvent Vakaru Bank.
- Prices for hot water have increased by 19.5 percent since August 1 when the government decided to raise the tariffs for heating, the Statistics Department reports.
- The Lithuanian Polish Election Action group will run for parliament with Russian and Belorussian public organizations at the elections in October.
- U.S. state officials who visited Vilnius on Saturday to introduce to Lithuanian diplomats the 'Baltic Action Plan' assured that this plan was not an alternative to membership in NATO.
- A survey by the prosecutor's office shows that illegal banking transactions and property frauds caused $19 million, 1.7 million German marks and 666 million litas of damage.
- The head of the Lithuanian Geology Service Gediminas Motuza says oil extracting has good prospects and that crude oil reserves in Lithuania could be worth some $1.0 billion.
- Lucent Technologies, a division of AT&T, won an international bid to modernise the interior ministry and the border police communication system for some $6.0 million.
- The largest Estonian bank Hansapank, which has a share capital of 180 million kroons, intends to open its office in Lithuania in two years at the latest.
